id: title:Piccirello:remove csp enforce other signed out pages flag

review.posthog_relevance: Changes Content Security Policy (CSP) enforcement behavior and configuration for PostHog Cloud and self-hosted instances, specifically removing a rollout flag and switching signed-out page enforcement from conditional to unconditional.
review.reason: The change removes a feature flag and associated rollout bucketing for CSP enforcement on signed-out pages, replacing it with unconditional enforcement for supported environments. This represents a substantive, bounded change to the security configuration and operational setup of PostHog Cloud and self-hosted deployments. review.uncertainty: The complete benefit and risk assessment is limited by the lack of runtime behavior and test results, and the removal of the rollout flag removes the ability to perform a gradual rollout or selective enforcement for signed-out pages.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, complete change group. No missing context or unrelated PRs detected. No score assigned; tier assignment requires a score, not an observation-only JSON.

observations.behavior: Documentation change: removed the statement that the app policy is enforced only for signed-in users; now says it is enforced for every visitor, signed-in or not.
observations.code_quote: - **The app policy** governs every SPA page. On PostHog Cloud and in local development, it is enforced for every visitor, signed-in or not. A self-hosted install only reports it, because its violations reach nobody. Embeddable documents, such as shared dashboards, always stay report-only.
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies CSP enforcement behavior for PostHog Cloud and local development, removing the distinction between signed-in and signed-out visitors. This could prevent future misunderstandings about when CSP enforcement applies, but does not change implementation.

observations.behavior: Removes the entire signed-out enforcement flag and its associated helper, including the feature-flag-dependent enforcement and the UUID-based bucketing for signed-out visitors.
observations.posthog_connection: Removes a rollout-flag-dependent enforcement path for signed-out pages. This could reduce configuration complexity and remove a potential failure mode where a flag lookup could leave enforcement report-only. However, the removal also removes the ability to selectively enforce for signed-out pages, which could change behavior for those visitors.

observations.behavior: Changes CSP enforcement for signed-out pages from flag-dependent to unconditional enforcement for non-hobby, non-self-hosted installs; removes the signed-out enforcement path and its helper.
observations.posthog_connection: Replaces the flag-dependent enforcement with unconditional enforcement for signed-out pages. This could increase security posture for signed-out visitors, but also removes the ability to opt-in enforcement for those pages. The removal of the UUID-based bucketing also removes the ability to do a rollout percentage for signed-out pages.
